campaigns.title: Help Gopalan of Akshaya Trust feed and care for rescued abandoned elderly parents
campaigns.description: “Parvathi Amma (name changed) was brought to Akshaya Trust by her son. He brought her here saying she was being taken to the hospital for treatment and he would be back in a while. It's been 8 years since that day. The phone number he gave to us was made up, even his address was false. Imagine the pain of the mother who was abandoned in such a heartless manner. She is not the only one. We have over 260 elderly parents here and most of them have faced abandonment, neglect or even abuse”, says G Gopalan, the founder of Akshaya Trust, the NGO taking care of abandoned seniors who have no one else in the world.Without Gopalan’s Akshaya Trust, countless elderly would still be on the streets or simply deprived of the love and care they deserve. The NGO takes care of every single need of its seniors from Food to medical care and housing. Your donation can enable Akshaya Trust to reach out to many more elderly with food and support. Contribute generously. Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).G Gopalan, a well-to-do businessman preferred to serve the elderly than living a peaceful retired life. He says that he was too shocked to see the state of the elderly, treated shabbily by their own children.A lifeline for hundreds of neglected elderlyToday, Akshaya Trust offers a safe haven to over 260 elderly parents, shielding them from the harsh realities of street life. This organization attends to all their needs, providing comprehensive medical care and ensuring they recover from past traumas. The trust also organises joyful celebrations during festivals and special occasions, bringing happiness into their lives.To date, Akshaya Trust has served over 1,000 elderly parents most of whom were from extremely weak financial backgrounds and had no way to fend for themselves. Akshaya Trust: A silver lining for elderlyAkshaya Trust’s efforts are a lifeline for these seniors, but they rely heavily on public support to continue. You can be the hero these elderly parents deserve. Donate now to help care for them.Your contribution can transform the lives of many homeless seniors. Support Akshaya Trust’s mission today.Donate to this fundraiser on Give.do, India’s largest and most trusted online donation platform, to help elderly parents abandoned by their children get the love and care they deserve.

campaigns.title: Help Maitri provide shelter and care to abandoned widow mothers
campaigns.description: In Vrindavan, thousands of elderly widow mothers face the harsh reality of abandonment and suffering. With no one to turn to, many are left begging on the streets, exposed to heat, cold and rain,Donate so that Maitri can provide shelter, food, clothes and medical support to abandoned elderly mothers now. Give generously.Lt Gen (Retd) Bhopinder Singn and his wife Winnie Singh and have witnessed many cases of widow mothers being abandoned on the streets of Vrindavan, one of the holiest places in India. “Children leave their mothers as soon as they become widows. The children start feeling the burden. This has become a practice in today's society that money comes first and everything else later,” says Winnie whose Maitri India, rescues widowed mothers from the streets of Vrindavan.Many widowed elderly mothers often end up living a lonely life and begging to survive on the streets. And Maitri aspires to take care of every widow in need of help, but because of lack of funds, Winnie and Maitri are in a position to do it. Gen Bhopinder Singh is like a brother to many widow mothers."Elderly widows don't have shelter. They sleep in cowsheds over sacks. They don't have a blanket. Nights are really difficult for them," shares Gen Bhopinder Singh.Maitri aims to:Provide shelter and nutritious meals leading to improved health and wellbeingMake physical and mental health services accessibleOffer necessary quality aged care and assisted living supportIncrease awareness and engagement around the struggles of abandoned widow mothersWhy donate to MaitriWinnie needs your support to help those in need of food, healthcare and well-being. “Maitri urgently needs your support to provide nutritious food, clothing and healthcare to sustain these widow mothers who are prone to more illnesses as they age,” appeals Winnie. “You can become the family they were denied. Hold their hands so they don't need to beg ever again,” says Gen Bhopinder Singh. Let’s rescue abandoned widows mothers from the streets of Vrindavan and give them a better future. Donate now.Our help will enable Maitri to save hundreds of abandoned widows from a life of begging, and restore the respect, dignity, and identity they deserve.

Our NGO partner Neptune Foundation has been a pillar of support for countless such abandoned grandparents, neglected and destitute senior citizens, helping them find something that many thought they had lost forever, a safe place to call homeThe NGO sustains its old age home through public support and is in urgent needs for donations and funds to keep the shelter going. Your donation can go a long way in giving these elderly parents the home they deserve. Donate generously!Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking.Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).A home when there is nowhere else to goNeptune Foundation provides free shelter, nutritious food, healthcare, companionship and emotional support to elderly people who have been abandoned, rejected or left without the means to care for themselves. Many residents are widowed, living alone, economically vulnerable, medically fragile or have experienced neglect and abuse.Today, 41 senior citizens between the ages of 60 and 95 live at the home. campaigns.title: Help Prasad provide shelter and care to orphaned kids and abandoned elderly parents
campaigns.description: Prasad and his wife Anu once had a daughter, little Prarthana , who passed away when she was still a toddler. Heartbroken but determined to honour her memory, they decided to dedicate their lives to those who had no one.  What began as adopting eight distressed children has now grown into a loving community that survives solely because Prasad refuses to give up. “My father, a farmer, ended his life owing to debt and distress. What I have faced as a child, I don't want any other child to face the same, and that is the biggest motivation. At present, we have 45 children and 25 abandoned elderly in our shelter home. We are their family. Anu (my wife) loves them like her own, and I provide for them and protect them like any father would,” says Prasad who stands as the last hope for these young ones and the elderly.  Unfortunately, he has been supporting this home with his meager earnings as an autorickshaw driver. He is in urgent need of help to keep a roof over his large family. You can lend him a hand in his noble work. Donate as much as you can today.Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).When pain became a missionPrasad knows what it means to grow up with hunger, fear, and the constant uncertainty of survival. He remembers the nights his family slept without food, the days his mother struggled alone after his father’s suicide, and the years he worked as a child doing menial jobs just to stay afloat. Today, those memories shape every decision he makes as the founder of Prathana Foundation, a home where abandoned elderly parents and orphaned children live together, as one family.“Our home is very unique. Here, orphans and elderly parents who have been abandoned by their children live together as a family. Here grandparents get the love of grandchildren, and orphaned kids are cared for by the elderly,” he shares with quiet pride.  In this one home, 45 children and 25 abandoned elderly have found love, belonging, and dignity, things life once denied them.But behind this warmth is a daily struggle that Prasad carries alone.  The daily struggle for survival“It’s very difficult for me to earn enough to sustain such a big home as an auto rickshaw driver. I am constantly in fear that if I run out of money, what will happen to the elderly and the orphans,” he says. The rising number of children and elderly people taking shelter here means more mouths to feed, more medicines to buy, more hospital visits, and more responsibilities on a man who already gives everything he has.Even after both he and Anu lost their jobs, he took up auto-rickshaw driving so the home could run. But the expenses of running such a large shelter are overwhelming.  Children need nutritious rations, school supplies, a safe environment, and emotional support. Elderly parents, many frail and chronically ill, need constant medical attention, medicines, and hospital visits. And the need keeps growing.I request you all to see these children and elderly as a member of your family and donate generously for them, so that their lives can be transformed,” Prasad appeals.Your support today can ensure- Daily nutritious meals for children and elderly parents  - Medical care, medicines, and emergency support for the elderly  - Safe shelter, clothing, and hygiene essentials  - Schooling, books, and basic education for every child  In a world where abandonment and loneliness break so many lives, Prathana Foundation stands as a rare home where forgotten grandparents and orphaned children rebuild hope together.  But this home, this family, cannot survive without you.  Your contribution can help Prasad continue saying “yes” to every abandoned child… every lonely elderly parent… every life that deserves love.  Donate today and help ensure that no elderly mother sleeps alone, no child suffers the scars Prasad once carried, and no family built on love collapses because of financial struggle.  Donate to this fundraiser on give.do, India’s most trusted online donation platform, to support Prathana Foundation in its mission to rescue and care for orphans of farmers and abandoned elderly. Your kindness can help keep this beautiful family together.

campaigns.title: Help Leena in saving girls from being lost forever in red-light areas
campaigns.description: "Hundreds of young girls are lost forever in the dark lanes of red-light areas," says Leena Kejriwal, the founder of Missing Link Trust. These girls endure unimaginable abuse and exploitation, being lured or trafficked into an industry that breaks them physically and emotionally. Missing Link Trust is on a mission to prevent the tragedy before it happens, and also rehabilitate girls and women who are rescued from forced sex work.Leena’s journey began with her powerful street art project in Kolkata, where she painted haunting silhouettes of missing girls to raise awareness against sex trafficking. Now, she leads a larger fight — one that focuses on prevention and rehabilitation. But this mission needs your support.You can save countless girl children from going missing forever. Donate now.Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).Preventing Trafficking Before It Begins“When girls come into a red-light area, the first thing is that they are broken, physically and emotionally,” Leena says. “It’s like they will be caught, hands and legs tied, and all heinous crimes committed on them.” These are the brutal realities that Missing Link Trust fights against every day.Many of these girls are from impoverished regions like the Sundarbans, and traffickers prey on their vulnerability. “It’s shocking that they sell themselves for as low as a hundred rupees,” Leena adds. "They ready her through violent acts, removing all threads of shame from her."But why wait until a girl is trafficked to save her? Missing Link Trust believes in stopping trafficking at its root — through “prevention, prevention, prevention” as Leena puts it. The goal is simple: protect girls from ever being lost to this darkness.A Safe World for Children“Our mission is the prevention of abuse and exploitation of children,” Leena emphasizes. “Our vision is to create a safe world for children, and we want to do this with a preventive methodology.”Every Donation MattersYour support will help Missing Link Trust continue its vital work of rescuing, rehabilitating, and preventing the trafficking of young girls. The funds raised will go directly towards:Prevention programs in vulnerable areas to stop trafficking before it happens.Rehabilitation services for girls rescued from red-light areas, providing them with medical care, emotional support, and education.Awareness campaigns to reach at-risk communities and ensure girls are protected from traffickers.Together, We Can Make a Difference“Why wait for a girl to get trafficked to save her?” asks Leena. With your help, we can stop this horror before it begins. Your donation will help us create a world where no girl is lost to the nightmare of trafficking.Donate to this fundraiser by Give, India’s largest and most trusted online giving platform, to support Missing Link Trust to save young girls from being trafficked and help rehabilitate those rescued.

campaigns.title: Gift education to underprivileged children
campaigns.description:
In India, socio-economic circumstances of a child strongly govern the type of school, education, and quality of life she will live. While enrollment in schools is common, the quality of education being provided is extremely poor, especially in the state of UP. ASER 2014 shows that 71% of class 8 children in UP cannot even read class 2 Hindi textbooks. These precious year spent in school with no learning is a huge loss to these underprivileged children and their families. Every child deserves access to quality education and healthcare to become contributing members of society and live a quality life. 
 E&H Foundation is enabling quality education for the underprivileged children in UP by researching and partnering with highly successful proven models on the ground and helping them scale up at a very low cost. Currently E&H Foundation has partnered with Gyanshala model that is helping children achieve grade appropriate learning in classes 1-4 at a low cost of ₹5000 per child per year compared to average government cost of ₹12000 per child. E&H Foundation also works to increase community engagement, liaison with the government, run advocacy programmes, as well as facilitate the implementing organisation to become sustainable. It takes only INR 10,000 annually to educate two children, and an annual contribution of 1 Lakh can take care of an entire classroom of 25 children. 
 Since its inception, E&H Foundation has provided quality education to 13000 children in 3 years for grades 1-4 in 3 districts of UP - Farrukhabad, Kanpur, and Lucknow. Independent studies show that the students have consistently attained grade appropriate learning scoring 100-­‐150% higher marks compared to government school children and almost comparable to India’s best CBSE schools at ₹5000 per child per year, creating scaling up potential. More than 55% students being educated by at such E&H Foundation sponsored classes are young girls, helping bridge the gap between male and female literacy rate.

campaigns.title: Project Nanhe Kalam
campaigns.description:
Primary rural education is suffering a major lag because of several issues. It is not only affecting the present society but the whole future of the community in question. Students are not getting ample opportunities, atmosphere and courage to succeed in life. It is very important for the society to formulate a system to envisage the hidden latent from primary rural students. It is important, not only to provide them quality education but also an atmosphere where they can get energised or motivated to build dreams. They are to be provided with a place where dreams can be turned into reality.  
 Self Reliant India is an organisation focussed to bring self reliance to each sector and community in the nation. We believe education can be the best weapon to develop self reliance. With aims intact, we started Project Nanhe Kalam, wherein students of primary rural government schools are coached for entrance exam of Navodhya schools. Navodhya Schools are a huge success and need no introduction. Induction of our students into these schools will provide them with an atmosphere to think out of the box and turn out as role models for their villages. Most importantly, the  teaching staff mainly consists of graduate youth who are preparing for government competitive exams. This way, even youths develop teaching ability.  
 Our work is affecting not only the students and the teachers, but the entire community. We have run this project for almost a year, and the results are overwhelmingly good. There was a selection of 20 students from SRI. The percentage of students getting selected to Navodhya (Rewari), who come from rural government schools, rose by 20% to 25% of the overall selections. This change has bought a ray of hope to villagers and communities are getting attracted to this program.
